title: Agents aren’t humans (but they kinda are)
contentSnippet: AI agents act for millions, but servers see intermediaries that strip user visibility. This post defines the problem space and introduces a collaborative approach to safely identifying, allowing, and managing this automated traffic.

title: Email threat landscape: Q3 2026 trends and insights
contentSnippet:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence observed a sharp rise in email-based phishing activity at the end of Q3 2026 (July – September), even as QR code phishing declined, CAPTCHA-gated phishing recovered, and malicious messages spoofing familiar business-service sender domains exposed risks associated with security overrides.
The post Email threat landscape: Q3 2026 trends and insights appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog.

title: Accessibility statements now have a home on GitHub
contentSnippet:
GitHub now highlights ACCESSIBILITY.md files and helps maintainers document accessibility goals, known barriers, supported environments, contributor expectations, and reporting processes.
The post Accessibility statements now have a home on GitHub appeared first on The GitHub Blog.

title: Want to Rent an Internet Address at the White House?
contentSnippet: Several staffers at the White House are using computers or mobile devices equipped with residential proxy services that render their internet address available for others to rent, security experts warned today. One of the proxy services is a Russian company whose founder's web hosting business was ground zero for cyberattacks against election systems in Arizona and Illinois in 2016.

title: Setting a new standard for responsible AI infrastructure
contentSnippet: OpenAI introduces its National Community Compact and Compute Campus Policy Blueprint to protect local resources, create jobs, and guide responsible AI infrastructure development.

title: Amazon S3 Tables now offer managed migration of Apache Hive tables to Apache Iceberg
contentSnippet: You can now migrate existing Apache Hive datasets in Amazon S3 to fully managed Apache Iceberg tables in Amazon S3 Tables, with no pipelines to build or compute to provision, while production workloads keep running.
